Share all information about your medications, including prescription and non-prescription drugs, as well as herbal products, with your doctor and pharmacist to ensure safe and effective use. 2. In the event of an overdose, if the individual exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, immediately call 911. If the symptoms are less severe, contact a poison control center without delay. U.S. residents can reach the poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. 3. While using this medication, your doctor may recommend laboratory or medical tests, such as kidney and liver function tests or blood counts, to monitor your health and the medication's effects. Ensure you attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. 4. If you miss a dose of this medication, it is crucial to consult your doctor or pharmacist promptly to establish a new dosing schedule. Do not attempt to double the dose to make up for the missed one. 5. For proper storage of this medication, refer to the product instructions or consult your pharmacist. Do not dispose of medications by flushing them down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Discard the medication appropriately when it is expired or no longer needed. 6. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about the product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or suitable for your specific condition. Always seek complete information and personalized advice from your healthcare professional regarding this medication and your health needs. 7. Before using lincomycin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, clindamycin, or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients, such as benzyl alcohol, which could cause allergic reactions or other complications. 8. Lincomycin may interfere with the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. Inform your healthcare provider if you are scheduled to receive any vaccinations. 9. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used if clearly necessary, as determined by your doctor. Additionally, this drug can pass into breast milk, so consult your healthcare provider if you are breastfeeding. 10. Drug interactions can alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a detailed list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal supplements, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. 11. Adding plans to your medication management allows you to compare formulary status with other drugs in the same class. To view formulary information, create a list of plans, which can be saved and edited at any time. Contact the applicable plan provider for the most current formulary information, as individual plans and details may vary. 12. If you send information about this product to another individual, ensure you have their permission to do so. By clicking send, you confirm that you are authorized to share this information.
